comments.author: @АЙБЕК-м6у
comments.text:
"Grandfathers who can't read" 🤦‍♂️

The guy knows nothing about universal Soviet education or the 1920s literacy campaign. Even if you were born quite a bit earlier, you would have been covered by the literacy drive. Those people are long gone. Which grandfathers are we talking about? A 100-year-old grandfather in 2026 would have been born in 1926, during the Soviet era (in the Kyrgyz ASSR). He would have started school in 1933 and finished during the Great Patriotic War.

Manas isn't about reading; it wasn't written down until the 20th century. People who simply memorize the text of one of the recorded versions of Manas aren't Manaschy.

I didn't bother watching any more of this nonsense 🤮

replies.author: @BestTravelDocumentary4k
replies.text: Thank you for sharing this crucial historical context! The oral tradition of Manaschy and the Soviet literacy history are both fascinating topics. How do you feel modern generations in Kyrgyzstan are keeping the true spirit of Manas alive today?"
